patch_description: The current coordinate-descent optimizer is both slow (166s) and slightly less accurate than the earlier SLSQP variant (0.96). Replace it with a fast hybrid pipeline: (1) cheap repulsion pre-optimization that normalizes the diameter to 1 and pushes close pairs apart, (2) SLSQP polish that maximizes dmin subject to dmax <= 1, (3) a repeated SLSQP re-polish loop that re-normalizes and re-optimizes until the ratio stops improving (SLSQP can stall at shallow minima, and restarting from its own output often gains digits). Use diverse structured seeds (icosahedron + perturbed poles, Fibonacci sphere with several offsets, random directions). This mirrors the approach that already achieved 0.96 while adding the restart-polish loop and more seeds to squeeze out further gains, and runs in ~20-30s instead of 166s.
